key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Right eye showed full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Vision loss occurred 10 days after initial presentation
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

raw.rationale: The presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm on vitreous biopsy, along with positive immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein, strongly supports the diagnosis of Astrocytoma.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did develop occlusion of the central retinal artery, this appears to be a secondary complication rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: Similar to central retinal artery occlusion, the central retinal vein occlusion seems to be a consequence of the underlying disease process rather than the primary cause.

rejected.label: Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings, including the focal enhancement along the enlarged right optic nerve on MRI, do not typically align with optic neuritis, which usually presents with pain on eye movement and a more acute onset of vision loss.

rejected.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: While ischemic optic neuropathy could explain some of the vision loss and optic disc swelling, the biopsy and immunohistochemistry results indicating an astrocytic neoplasm point towards a neoplastic process rather than an ischemic event as the primary diagnosis.
